topic: Stranded in the desert with one bottle of water: save it or drink it?
title: Stranded In The Desert
idea: Water saves you in your body, not in the bottle: sip early and often, and ration your sweat instead.
hook: Your car just died in the desert. You have one bottle of water.

beats.line: Do you save it, or drink it?
In this heat, you can sweat out a liter every hour.
Instinct says save it. But ration it, and the heat can take you down with water still in the bottle.
So sip it, early and often. Water works in your body, not in the bottle.
Don't ration your water. Ration your sweat.
One. Cover up. Clothes block the sun and make your sweat last.
Two. Find shade, and get off the ground. The sand is far hotter than the air.
Three. Stay with the car. It's much easier to spot than you.

end.line: So, save it or drink it? Tell me which one you picked.

description: Stranded in the desert with one bottle of water: save it or drink it? Most people pick wrong.

facts.claim: In desert heat a person can sweat out a liter or more per hour (walking ~1.2 L/h; FM gives up to 2.5-3.5 L/h in extreme heat).
facts.source: US Army Survival Manual FM 21-76 / FM 3-05.70, ch. 13 Desert Survival (sjsu.edu/people/michelle.hager/docs/fm_21-76_us_army_survival_manual_2006.pdf)

facts.claim: Rationing water makes you a likely heat casualty even while you still have water ('Do not ration your water! If you try to ration water, you stand a good chance of becoming a heat casualty').
facts.source: US Army Survival Manual FM 21-76 / FM 3-05.70, ch. 13 Desert Survival (sjsu.edu/people/michelle.hager/docs/fm_21-76_us_army_survival_manual_2006.pdf)

facts.claim: Sip at regular intervals, do not wait for thirst ('Thirst is not a reliable guide'; 'even when not thirsty, drink small amounts of water at regular intervals').
facts.source: US Army Survival Manual FM 21-76 / FM 3-05.70, ch. 13 Desert Survival (sjsu.edu/people/michelle.hager/docs/fm_21-76_us_army_survival_manual_2006.pdf)

facts.claim: 'Conserve sweat not water' / 'Ration your sweat, not your water'.
facts.source: US Army Survival Manual FM 21-76 / FM 3-05.70, ch. 13 Desert Survival (sjsu.edu/people/michelle.hager/docs/fm_21-76_us_army_survival_manual_2006.pdf); USMC FMFRP 0-53 Afoot in the Desert (contents)

facts.claim: Stay fully clothed: clothing keeps the sun off and holds sweat against the skin for its full cooling effect.
facts.source: US Army Survival Manual FM 21-76 / FM 3-05.70, ch. 13 Desert Survival (sjsu.edu/people/michelle.hager/docs/fm_21-76_us_army_survival_manual_2006.pdf)

facts.claim: Desert sand and rock average 16-22 C hotter than the air (air 43 C, sand may be 60 C); put something between you and the ground.
facts.source: US Army Survival Manual FM 21-76 / FM 3-05.70, ch. 13 Desert Survival (sjsu.edu/people/michelle.hager/docs/fm_21-76_us_army_survival_manual_2006.pdf)

facts.claim: Stay with your vehicle: it gives shade and you will be found more easily.
facts.source: US National Park Service, Death Valley, 2016 (nps.gov/deva/learn/news/remote-travel-in-summer-heat.htm)

factcheck.note: Povodna veta 'people have died of thirst with water still in the bottle' sa nedala dolozit primarnym zdrojom -> nahradena tvrdenim z FM 21-76. 'Drink when thirsty' nahradene 'sip early and often'.
